sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four useful ways to get started

examples.heading: A short metric trip
examples.text: 100 km at 8 L/100 km uses 8 litres. At 1.50 per litre, the cost is 12.00 USD.

examples.heading: Include the return journey
examples.text: The same one-way inputs with Return journey selected use 16 litres and cost 24.00 USD.

examples.heading: Keep US gallons consistent
examples.text: 300 miles at 30 US MPG uses 10 US gallons. At 3.50 per gallon, the cost is 35.00 USD.

examples.heading: Use an imperial pump price
examples.text: 200 miles at 40 imperial MPG uses 5 imperial gallons. At 7.00 per gallon, the cost is 35.00 GBP.

steps.heading: Choose the question
steps.text: Select the mode that matches your task. The input labels follow that choice.

steps.heading: Enter the values
steps.text: Match the pump-price unit to the selected fuel unit. Currency is a label, not a live exchange-rate conversion.

steps.heading: Check the result
steps.text: Calculate, inspect the working and save the result if needed. Cancel stops a long job.

method.heading: The method behind this result
paragraphs: Metric consumption states litres used per one hundred kilometres. Fuel used is distance × consumption / 100. Multiply that fuel quantity by the price per litre to estimate the cost. A higher L/100 km figure therefore means more fuel for the same trip.

MPG states miles travelled per gallon. Fuel used is distance / MPG, then cost is gallons × price per gallon. A higher MPG figure means less fuel for the same distance. This is the inverse direction of a litres-per-distance measure.

US gallons and imperial gallons are different quantities. Select the correct MPG mode and use a pump price for the same gallon type. The calculator does not silently mix one gallon definition with another or convert a price whose unit is unknown.

Return journey doubles the entered one-way distance before calculating fuel. Enter the one-way distance even when that option is selected. If the return route has a different length or consumption, calculate each leg separately and combine the amounts.

Passenger share divides the complete trip cost by the positive whole number of people sharing it. Include the driver when the driver pays a share. Displayed money and shares round independently to two places, so rounded shares may differ from the total by a small remainder.

The arithmetic is exact for the entered decimals, but a trip estimate is only as realistic as its assumptions. Traffic, route, load, weather and driving style can change consumption. No live fuel prices, route service or exchange-rate API is used.

uses.heading: Use the result with the right assumptions
paragraphs: Use a recent consumption figure from the relevant driving conditions rather than assuming a laboratory rating will match every journey. Check whether a vehicle display uses US or imperial MPG before choosing the mode.

For a shared trip, agree what costs are included. This estimate covers the entered fuel only, not tolls, parking, wear, insurance or a formal reimbursement rate. Add other agreed costs separately rather than disguising them as extra fuel consumption.

Zero distance or a zero pump price is valid and gives zero cost. Efficiency must remain positive, and the number of people must be a positive whole number. Impossible inputs clear the old result instead of leaving an unrelated estimate visible.

privacy.heading: Private calculations, clear limits
paragraphs: Your inputs and results stay in this browser. Calculation runs in a local worker, without a calculation API or uploaded data.
The page saves only your theme preference. A copied link contains the selected inputs and options, so share it deliberately.
Large calculations depend on device time and memory. Cancel stops the active job. An error clears old answers and disables their downloads.

faq.question: Which units can I use?
faq.answer: Kilometres with L/100 km, miles with US MPG, or miles with imperial MPG. The pump-price unit must match the chosen mode.

faq.question: Are US and imperial gallons interchangeable?
faq.answer: No. Select the correct gallon type and use a price for that same unit. A mismatched price gives a wrong trip estimate.

faq.question: Should I enter one-way or total distance?
faq.answer: Enter one-way distance when using Return journey. That option doubles it. Enter the full journey only when One-way journey is selected.

faq.question: Can I split the cost between passengers?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter the number of people sharing the complete cost, including the driver if the driver pays a share.

faq.question: Why do rounded shares not always sum exactly?
faq.answer: Each share is rounded independently to two places. Splitting a total into several parts can leave a small rounding remainder.

faq.question: Does changing the currency convert the price?
faq.answer: No. It changes the currency label only. Enter the actual pump price in the currency you intend to use.

faq.question: Does this fetch current fuel prices?
faq.answer: No. All prices and consumption values come from your inputs. There is no route, price or exchange-rate API call.

faq.question: Can I enter a free-fuel or zero-distance case?
faq.answer: Yes. Zero price or distance gives zero cost. Fuel efficiency must still be positive, and the passenger count must be a positive integer.

faq.question: Does the estimate include tolls or vehicle wear?
faq.answer: No. It estimates fuel only. Add other agreed costs separately for a complete travel budget.

faq.question: Will the car use exactly this amount?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Real consumption changes with conditions. The result is an estimate from the values you provide.
